title: Bittensor Daily News: November 28, 2026

updates.headline: SN64 Chutes says Gamma payments are live and names operating-company CEO
updates.summary: In a November 27 team statement, SN64 Chutes says Gamma can now pay for all its services, with alpha burned through the protocol. Fiat conversion remains unresolved: the team says legal, tax and conversion arrangements are still being worked through. It is also narrowing its model catalog to concentrate compute on its most-used models and adding uncensored options. CJ (@cjh247) has joined as CEO of the operating company, while Jon remains focused on building Chutes. TEE-secured virtual machines, containers and sandboxes are next, with beta signups open and miner onboarding targeted for year-end. Those infrastructure milestones remain plans. Finalized Gamma records show three SN64 spending events totaling about 1.21 service credits on November 27 Eastern. That confirms small-scale recorded use, not independent customer identities, meaningful adoption scale or completed VM deployment.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: a substantive payment and operating-company update affects a major inference service. Five is not established by announced availability without evidence of exceptional new adoption.

updates.headline: SN53 engy pins miner builds to reduce version drift
updates.summary: SN53 engy merged a release-control change on November 27 that identifies the exact miner file by commit and checksum. Its provisioning path is intended to install that file and reject a checksum mismatch, while miners report a fingerprint of the file actually running. The change is described as one part of a three-part rollout, so the merge alone does not establish that every miner has upgraded. It addresses version consistency, not evidence of a cause for the token’s price move.
updates.ratingReason: Two stars: a useful reliability change with a limited, clearly documented scope.

updates.headline: SN28 SayGM offers one matched top-up through November 30
updates.summary: SN28 SayGM’s November 27 offer matches one top-up of $10 to $100 with the same amount in service credit. The team says new and existing accounts qualify, with one matched top-up per person, through the end of Monday, November 30. A $100 top-up therefore gives $200 of spending credit under the stated promotion. This is credit for using the service, not a cash payout or token return. updates.headline: SN56 Gradients plans lower entry fees and a new reward split for December 7
updates.summary: SN56 Gradients published incoming tournament changes on November 28 for December 7. Guaranteed shares are planned at 25% for text, 15% for compression and 15% for image, with the participation-based portion rising from 25% to 45%. Participation will count miners that beat the incumbent in round one, rather than registrations. A new winner initially receives 85% of its tournament share; successive defenses gradually reduce that to 60%, leaving 30% for second and 10% for third. Text entry falls from 0.7 to 0.6 TAO and compression from 0.6 to 0.5 TAO; image stays at 0.4 TAO. The source marks this in progress and not yet shipped.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: specific reward and entry-cost changes affect miner participation; these remain scheduled competition mechanics.

updates.headline: SN14 Cacheon opens wider inference optimization and an H200 arena
updates.summary: In a November 26 merge, SN14 Cacheon expanded what miners can optimize: model operations, prefix caching, queue order and selected scheduling decisions can now be submitted together. It also added an Inkling 2 Mini arena on H200 hardware. The maintainer says this version was deployed on mainnet that day. Submissions remain subject to quality and state checks; a faster result alone is not enough. This is a dated catch-up on a concrete competition expansion, separate from the unverified burn amount circulating in tracker posts.

updates.headline: SN39 Kokoah completes a 167.795 TAO purchase and alpha burn
updates.summary: SN39 Kokoah announced its first buyback on November 28. The cited finalized transaction records 167.795 TAO entering an add-stake-and-burn operation and 24,414.038521254 SN39 alpha burned, with successful dispatch. That independently supports the purchase-and-burn execution, rather than just a promise. Kokoah says the funds came from 15 days of revenue and covered more than 55% of mining rewards; the revenue attribution and coverage calculation remain team-reported. It also says it will increase buyback frequency. The chain event does not by itself establish the origin of the revenue or guarantee future purchases.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: a completed, independently checked purchase and burn is a material operating milestone. Five is not justified by one bounded transaction or unverified revenue-coverage claims.

updates.headline: SN50 Synth changes payout timing and fixes launch-period scoring
updates.summary: SN50 Synth’s published validator rules reached version 1.11 on November 28. From 14:00 UTC, the rules pay only fully matured scoring blocks: two hours after a one-hour block ends and 26 hours after a 24-hour block ends. The operator warns this can cause a one-time change in weights. Further changes correct registration tracking, restore the intended launch ramp for six registrations and prevent early launch blocks from turning into later debt. A public-table publishing failure was also fixed without changing scoring. These changes describe this validator’s reward calculation, not a claim that every validator runs the same implementation. The rules distribute miner emissions among earning pots; they do not promise returns to all alpha holders.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: a concrete operational or product update, with the limits of the available evidence stated.

updates.headline: SN81 Reliquary merges groundwork for a public environment catalog
updates.summary: SN81 Reliquary merged code on November 28 allowing a qualified customer-created environment to be published with a license and source provenance. The design lets other accounts order evaluation, batch or reinforcement-learning work against that version and pay its scoring costs. An owner can later unlist a public version, but existing orders retain access. The merge lays groundwork for importing environments from Hugging Face and Prime Hub. Crucially, the change states that nothing is deployed and customer environments remain disabled, so this is development progress rather than a launched marketplace.

updates.headline: SN25 UR adds controls for shared bandwidth and monthly data
updates.summary: SN25 UR merged provider controls on November 28 that let hosts cap sharing speed and monthly data usage. Reaching the monthly allowance pauses sharing until the next UTC calendar month; limits and usage survive restarts and updates. A host’s allowance is divided across its provider slots and operators, rather than being duplicated for each one. The documentation warns that sharing less can reduce reliability ranking and earnings. This is a verified code change; deployment across the provider fleet has not been independently checked.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: practical host controls address bandwidth costs and participation constraints; fleet-wide rollout is not yet established.

updates.headline: SN13 Data Universe fixes score resets after miner re-registration
updates.summary: SN13 Data Universe merged a validator correction on November 27 so a changed registration block resets a miner’s scores even when its hotkey appears unchanged. The earlier rule only reacted to hotkey changes and could retain old scores after re-registration. Maintainers report that their historical replay reset all 12 tested renewals, while the old rule caught two. The patch compares consecutive syncs, so a renewal during validator downtime remains a stated limitation. This concerns miner registration within SN13, not re-registration of the subnet itself.

updates.headline: SN116 Carbon announces miner hold bonuses and a community treasury
updates.summary:
SN116 Carbon announced on November 27 that it is changing where declining miner rewards go. Its existing challenge rewards still halve every 24 hours. Under the announced distribution order, current winners are paid first, followed by bonuses for past winners who retain their earned alpha, a capped community treasury, and finally the remaining burn allocation. The aim is to reward continued participation instead of sending all of the declining allocation directly to burn.

The team says eligible winners can earn up to an additional 50% over a rolling 30-day window. Selling, unstaking or transferring the earned alpha reduces eligibility, reaching zero when half or more is gone; the lowest balance during the window counts. These are the announced rules, not a guaranteed return for general token holders.

Carbon describes a community council controlling treasury spending and says its own keys are excluded from bonuses, council seats and treasury payouts. Although the announcement says the mechanism has shipped, the public council page checked on November 28 still states that production admission is disabled and launch dates are unset. Completed treasury activation, live bonus payments and enforcement of the exclusions have not been independently verified.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: a concrete change to competition reward distribution affects miner participation. Four is not established for this bounded incentive update with treasury activation still unresolved.

updates.headline: SN122 CookingTAO reports four running miner integrations in beta
updates.summary: SN122 CookingTAO reported on November 28 that 23 miner-code submissions had produced nine published integrations, four running smoothly and two described by the team as profitable. Its interface is intended to let users participate in subnet mining from a TAO wallet. The team expects to complete beta in the coming weeks and is preparing CookingTAO Studio. The post does not provide the cost basis behind profitability, so those two reported cases should not be treated as a general return estimate. A full-launch date has not been confirmed.

updates.headline: SN35 becomes TTedu, rewarding tutor agencies for live teaching
updates.summary: Telureo announced on November 27 that it had acquired SN35 and introduced TTedu, an education subnet built around free public live lectures. A later official post said TTedu was open, and its public repository identifies the current SN35 project and its participation rules. Miners act as tutor agencies, each supporting up to five tutors. Validators score live watch-minutes rather than replay views, using a defined scoring window and excluding stale audience readings. The first phase centers on human teaching; personalized one-to-one and advanced AI tutoring are later plans. This is a substantive project transition, not a cosmetic contact update. Acquisition terms, sale price and the claimed commercial agreement have not been independently verified.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: a verified substantive project transition and a different participation model meet the standing identity-change rule. Five is not established by the initial teaching program.

updates.headline: SN99 Axonry releases a new small-model checkpoint with mixed benchmark results
updates.summary: SN99 Axonry has published its PR171 Qwen3.5-0.8B checkpoint and a model card with November 27 evaluation results. Compared with its earlier PR81 checkpoint, the team reports structured-output performance rising from 16.85% to 28.95% on IFStruct and GPQA Diamond from 34.72% to 37.25%. The same comparison shows IFBench falling from 35.00% to 24.67%, so the evidence is not an across-the-board improvement. The checkpoint changes existing weights without adding parameters or inference-time tools. Its card labels the scores self-reported and notes that the available runs are community results without a verification token. This is a downloadable research artifact with disclosed tradeoffs, not an independently reproduced benchmark victory.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: a public model artifact and documented evaluation tradeoffs provide substantive research news. Four is not established by self-reported bounded benchmarks.

updates.headline: SN113 Elo publishes a browser-speed competition for AI agents
updates.summary: SN113 Elo published its subnet repository on November 28 after its new identity appeared the previous day. The project is building a browser for AI agents: miners improve its open-source agent layer, while validators compare submissions with a pinned baseline on the same tasks and hardware. Submissions must first complete the tasks correctly, then compete on speed. The browser itself is closed source; the competition’s agent layer is MIT-licensed. This establishes the project’s published participation model, not independent evidence of customer adoption or a completed subnet sale.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: a previously unidentified slot now has a substantive verified project identity and an inspectable operating design; adoption and commercial execution do not support five.

ecosystem.headline: Federation announces $17,000 hackathon across three builder tracks
ecosystem.summary: Federation’s November 27 announcement offers $17,000 across three Bittensor hackathon tracks: $11,000 for building a subnet, $3,000 for developer tools and $3,000 for applications using existing subnet services. The announced deadline is January 12, 2027. Solo entrants and teams of up to five can participate, and hub membership is not required. France, China and India hubs are involved, with HackQuest support. These are announced competition terms and prize allocations, not prizes already awarded.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Three stars: a substantive builder opportunity, subject to the standing competition cap.

ecosystem.headline: Const argues for broader revenue accounting and discusses basket-yield assumptions
ecosystem.summary: In November 27 replies, Const argued that root distributions should be included when comparing Bittensor’s economic activity with other chains. He also cited annualized basket-yield estimates of 25% to 63%, explicitly assuming stable combined subnet prices, versus roughly 5% for standard TAO staking. These are his accounting argument and conditional estimates, not a newly verified external-revenue total or a demonstrated annual return. Protocol distributions and customer purchases measure different flows, so this report does not combine them into an independently verified revenue ranking.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Two stars: relevant ecosystem commentary with explicit assumptions, rather than a new executed protocol change.
